summary.name: Warden
summary.one_liner: Warden is a free, open-source native macOS chat app, built in SwiftUI, that lets you talk to many AI models (cloud and local) using your own API keys.
use_cases: chat with several AI providers from one Mac app
run local models through Ollama or LM Studio
ask questions about PDFs and CSV files
compare responses from multiple models side by side
use a private, offline-friendly AI chat on macOS
summary.what_it_does: Warden is a native macOS AI chat client built with SwiftUI. It supports many providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), xAI, Google Gemini, Perplexity, Groq, Mistral, Deepseek, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, and any OpenAI-compatible API, using your own API keys. You can drag and drop files such as PDF, CSV, and text to ask questions about them. A beta multi-model compare feature sends a prompt to up to three models at once. Chats can be organized into projects, and custom assistants (personas) can be created with set roles and tones. It also offers web search with citations, per-message tool toggles, optional MCP agents, and a menu bar mode.
notable: Built entirely in SwiftUI as a native macOS app, under 20MB, with zero telemetry
Supports local models via Ollama and LM Studio as well as many cloud providers
Multi-model compare (beta) across up to 3 models at once
Source code on GitHub under Apache 2.0; the Gumroad page is an optional donation page
caveats: The Gumroad page is only for optional support; the full app is free on GitHub with no paid tier
Cloud providers require the user's own API keys
The developer says this is their first Swift app and bugs are still being fixed
